title: lcw-evo-championship
label: Duel

won.source: Dawning's own Match 6 video-package recap: "cut to a shot of the closing moments of the Rook Black/Duel Evo Title match from Impulse 1.3, with Duel choking out the Texan to win the championship." Quoted verbatim and not resolved further — the source's own wording ("Evo Title match") is the only citation for this reign, kept exactly as written rather than silently normalized.

how: Choked Rook Black out at "Impulse 1.3" (a show this pass never located a separate document for). Lost the title before Dawning; the transition to Doctor David Chambers is undocumented in the surviving record and is left an honest gap rather than guessed.
note: GAP: no document records how or when Chambers won the title from Duel.

title: lcw-evo-championship
label: Rook Black

won.source: The wing's own founding status box of 28 October 2001 ("neo Title - Rook Black"), read alongside its own 21 October 2001 opening post — no title change is recorded between the two.

how: Still champion on the 13 December 2001 card, defending against Mike Static (result not captured). Lost the title to Duel afterward — see the following reign's own note.

title: lcw-evo-championship
label: Doctor David Chambers

won.source: Already champion by Dawning; no won-date survives (see the prior reign's own GAP note).

how: Retained over Brad Case (No Contest, Impulse 1.9) and Dean Wallace (submission, Dawning, 41:02); named Michael Gabrielle the #1 contender at the close of Impulse 2.1 — still champion when the surviving record ends.

title: lcw-evo-madhouse-championship
label: Duel

won.source: The wing's own founding status box of 28 October 2001 ("Hardcore Title - Duel"), read alongside the split itself (the belt renamed the day neo opened).

how: Defended against Gryfon on the wing's own first card (30 October 2001) and against Frank Heimdal on the 13 December 2001 card — both billed-only, no result captured, so retained by default rather than asserted. Lost the belt to Frank Heimdal in a cage match at Dawning (32:14), explicitly billed "the second Madhouse Champion in Evo history," confirming this was the first reign.

title: lcw-evo-madhouse-championship
label: Frank Heimdal

won.source: Dawning, Match 6, cage match, pinfall via a second Cranial Smoke; "Winner and NEW Madhouse Champion: Frank Heimdal (Match Time: 32:14)."

how: Still champion when the surviving record ends; a title defense against Gryfon (a ladder match) was previewed for the never-aired Impulse 2.2.
